'''Cameron Gib Luxton''' (born 1988 or 1989) is a New Zealand politician. He was elected to the [[New Zealand House of Representatives]] in the 2023 general election as an [[ACT New Zealand]] list Member of Parliament.

==Early life==
Luxton was raised in the Tauranga suburb of [[Papamoa]] and attended [[Mount Maunganui College]]. He spent seven years on a [[dairy farm]] in [[Galatea, New Zealand|Galatea]], during which he won Modern Apprentice of the Year in Rotorua at the Dairy Industry Awards in 2013 and Bay of Plenty Dairy Trainee in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://theweekendsun.co.nz/news/8992-getting-on-act.html |title=Getting in on the ACT |date=29 May 2020 |work=[[The Weekend Sun]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.farmersweekly.co.nz/news/everything-falling-his-way/ |title=Everything falling his way |work=Farmers Weekly |publisher=AgriHQ |date=4 April 2014 |accessdate=17 October 2023}}</ref> He has also worked as a self-employed builder.<ref name=":0" />

Luxton resides in Papamoa with his wife, Susan, and their two children.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/464843/builder-to-stand-for-act-in-tauranga-by-election |title=Builder to stand for Act in Tauranga by-election |date=7 April 2022 |publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]] |accessdate=17 October 2023}}</ref>

Luxton contested {{NZ electorate link|Tauranga}} in the {{NZ election link|2020}}. Originally at 16 on the ACT party list, he was bumped up to 15 after Pakuranga candidate [[Stephen Berry (politician)|Stephen Berry]] withdrew his nomination.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Vita Molyneux |date=6 July 2020 |title=ACT candidate Stephen Berry resigns due to 'exhaustion' from campaign preparation |language=en |work=[[Newshub]] |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/07/act-candidate-stephen-berry-resigns-due-to-exhaustion-from-campaign-preparation.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200706164810/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/07/act-candidate-stephen-berry-resigns-due-to-exhaustion-from-campaign-preparation.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=6 July 2020 |access-date=16 November 2023}}</ref> He came fourth in Tauranga, receiving 3.97% of the vote, and his list placement was not high enough to enter parliament.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gavin Ogden |date=16 November 2023 |title=Local Focus: Cameron Luxton on Candidate Camera |language=en-NZ |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/bay-of-plenty-times/news/local-focus-cameron-luxton-on-candidate-camera/ENQKZ6FO6APHPSDRNUUZD5TFJQ/ |access-date=16 November 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=New Zealand Electoral Commission |date=2020 |title=Electorate results: Tauranga |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-52.html}}</ref>

Following National MP [[Simon Bridges]]' announcement in March 2022 that he would resign, Luxton stated his intention to contest the [[2022 Tauranga by-election|resulting by-election]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Tauranga byelection candidates step forward to fill Simon Bridges' shoes |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/bay-of-plenty-times/news/tauranga-byelection-candidates-step-forward-to-fill-simon-bridges-shoes/2X4UFVPLQZY4ENJI3D3GAWJJTA/ |date=17 March 2022 |work=[[Bay of Plenty Times]] |publisher=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |first=Sandra |last=Conchie |url-access=subscription}}</ref> His candidacy was confirmed on 7 April.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/bay-of-plenty/128297242/luxton-to-stand-for-act-in-tauranga-byelection |title=Luxton to stand for ACT in Tauranga by-election |date=7 April 2022 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |first=Dan |last=Sheridan}}</ref> During the campaign, he likened [[Tauranga City Council#Crown commission|Tauranga commission chair]] [[Anne Tolley]] to former French queen [[Marie Antoinette]] and stated "It's time Tauranga gave her the same treatment. The power has gone to her head, and we say off with it."<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/bay-of-plenty/128699219/act-defend-tauranga-candidate-after-off-with-her-head-comment-aimed-at-tolley |title=ACT defend Tauranga candidate after 'off with her head' comment aimed at Tolley |first=Dan |last=Sheridan |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=19 May 2022 |accessdate=17 October 2022}}</ref> He finished third in the election with 10.2% of the vote.<ref name="2022 by-election result">{{cite web|url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/2022_tauranga_byelection/ |title=Tauranga – Official Result |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |date=1 July 2022 |access-date=2 July 2022 }}</ref>

In the [[2023 New Zealand general election|2023 general election]], Luxton was placed at number 11 on the ACT party list. He also contested the electorate of [[Bay of Plenty (New Zealand electorate)|Bay of Plenty]], coming third place. He was elected as a [[list MP]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/bay-of-plenty-times/news/election-results-2023-new-act-list-mp-cameron-luxton-bay-of-plenty-heads-to-parliament/RKJ4UGSXMZH7RDADPEG7QHWMKA/ |title=Election results 2023: New Act list MP Cameron Luxton, Bay of Plenty, heads to Parliament |first=Sandra |last=Conchie |work=[[Bay of Plenty Times]] |publisher=[[NZME]] |date=17 October 2023 |accessdate=17 October 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Bay of Plenty - Official Result |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-03.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=25 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123104114/https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-03.html |archive-date=23 November 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> After the election, Luxton was appointed the ACT spokesperson for conservation, housing, building and construction, infrastructure, local government, and transport. He was also appointed to the transport and infrastructure committee and the health committee.<ref name="New Zealand Parliament p085">{{cite web |title=Luxton, Cameron |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/members-of-parliament/luxton-cameron/ |access-date=12 April 2024 |website=New Zealand Parliament}}</ref>

On 11 April 2024, Luxton's [[private member's bill]] to remove restrictions on selling alcohol over Easter was selected for debate.<ref name="RNZ 2024 b513">{{cite news |date=11 April 2024 |title=Bill to remove Easter alcohol restrictions drawn from ballot |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/514012/bill-to-remove-easter-alcohol-restrictions-drawn-from-ballot |access-date=12 April 2024 |work=[[RNZ]] }}</ref> The bill was first debated on 17 December 2024 and was defeated by a margin of 74 to 49 votes; with MPs being granted a [[conscience vote]] on the matter.<ref>{{cite news |title=Easter trading: ACT MP 'surprised' as bill voted down |url=https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/on-air/matt-heath-tyler-adams-afternoons/audio/cameron-luxton-act-mp-on-parliament-voting-down-easter-trading-bill/ |access-date=21 December 2024 |work=[[Newstalk ZB]] |date=18 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241218020351/https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/on-air/matt-heath-tyler-adams-afternoons/audio/cameron-luxton-act-mp-on-parliament-voting-down-easter-trading-bill/ |archive-date=18 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Repeal of Good Friday and Easter Sunday as Restricted Trading Days (Shop Trading and Sale of Alcohol) Amendment Bill — First Reading |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20241217_20241218_16 |publisher=[[New Zealand Parliament]] |access-date=21 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241221035943/https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20241217_20241218_16 |archive-date=21 December 2024 |date=17 December 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In mid-April 2026, Luxton introduced a member's bill seeking to ban unelected appointees on local council committees from having voting rights. In addition, ACT leader [[David Seymour]] confirmed that the party would campaign on passing Luxton's bill within the first 100 days if re-elected following the [[2026 New Zealand general election]]. [[ACT Local]] councillor Davina Smolders had earlier clashed with [[Mayor of the Far North]] [[Moko Tepania]] for expanding the number of  [[Māori people|Māori]] [[iwi]] (tribal) and [[hapu]] (clan) representatives on the [[Far North District Council]]'s Te Kuaka Māori Strategic Relationships Committee.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Palmer |first1=Russell |title=ACT would ban voting rights for unelected appointees on local council committees if elected |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/top/592583/act-would-ban-voting-rights-for-unelected-appointees-on-local-council-committees-if-elected |access-date=19 April 2026 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=16 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260419224621/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/top/592583/act-would-ban-voting-rights-for-unelected-appointees-on-local-council-committees-if-elected |archive-date=19 April 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>
